parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is an Express HTTP adapter, and that is transport work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer. It only does four kinds of work: (1) it sets up the app, the routers and the middleware, (2) it parses and checks the shape of incoming data such as the request body, query values, path parameters, ISO dates and status text, (3) it passes each request to an application service (UserService, ProjectService, TaskService), and (4) it turns domain errors into HTTP status codes. It has no business rules or domain checks. For example, it doesn't decide whether a task can be assigned or marked done; it leaves those calls to the services. parseStatus only cleans up the status text the client sends and checks it with the domain's own isTaskStatus helper. The defaults it fills in (an empty description, a null assignee) are about turning a request into a call, not business policy. There is no persistence logic in the file.
